title: Design step: UX and architecture proposed after Gate 1, before the plan
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04; owner chose to include this step).

VISION journey step 4 'UX and architecture' and the next-milestone sentence 'creates the architecture and UX' - re-measured 2026-09-04: nothing exists between the Gate 1 approval and the decomposition run; the compiler seat plans straight from the approved contract (orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts, planning/compile-dispatcher.ts, planning/node-mission-producer.ts; seat reads `product_contract.read` and paged `documents_source_read`, PR #19).

FEATURE: a DESIGN planning step between Gate 1 and the plan. The wrapper staffs a design seat whose mission reads the approved contract and the PRD and submits a versioned DESIGN through a new MCP command `design.submit {goalRef, revision}`: screens/journey map (journey -> screens -> states), data model (entities, fields, relations), API surface (routes, payloads), component list, non-functional decisions (auth, accessibility, performance budgets), open decisions for the human. Durable aggregate `design:<goalId>` with versions; `design.read {goalRef}` for seats and the operator read `/design/read`. The human sees the Design on the goal and may request changes (comment-driven resubmit -> version bump) or accepts it implicitly by approving the plan - the plan-approval card names the design version the plan was compiled against. The compiler mission carries the design ref and its sections; node missions cite the screens/entities they implement. The step is skippable per goal ('plan without a design' toggle) so the loop never blocks on it.

Profile: TypeScript web app (React, Node, PostgreSQL) per VISION 'one controlled product profile first'.
definitionOfDone: `design.submit` (seat) and `design.read` (seat + operator) published with the full roster backfill; `design.submit` refuses DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED, DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID (exact-key roster), DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT - each asserted with code + layer; roster tests are bidirectional.

The wrapper staffs the design step after Gate 1 and before decomposition; e2e over a REAL daemon with a scripted seat double submits a design, and the compiler mission bytes then contain the design ref plus the five section headings (assert on the produced mission text).
The opened goal shows a Design tab with the five sections and the version; a resubmit bumps the version and the plan-approval card names the version the plan compiled against.
The per-goal 'plan without a design' toggle skips the step: test shows the decomposition run opens with no design and the mission states it.
Live drive on UnAI or a fresh project: a real seat submits a design - transcript + design ref in a row comment; VISION/README journey step 4 marked as running.
Gates quoted with their count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.

implementationPlan.description: ADVERSARIAL PASS OVER THE COMPOSED FEATURE, recorded in a step note — the integration read only the parent can do. (a) IS THE DESIGN LOAD-BEARING, or decorative? Trace one entity from the design aggregate into the compiler mission bytes and then into a node mission. A design that nothing downstream reads is a form the operator fills in twice and the plan ignores — that is the failure mode this whole feature risks, and child 2's mission assertions are the only thing preventing it. (b) DOES THE LOOP EVER BLOCK? Confirm a goal can always reach a plan: the skip toggle works, and a design step that is offered but never staffed (no seat available) does not wedge the goal. (c) THE SKIP PATH END TO END: a goal planned without a design must say so in the compiler mission AND on the approval card — confirm both, since a silent absence lets a seat and a human each assume the other saw one. (d) VERSION DRIFT: if a design is resubmitted AFTER the plan compiled, does the approval card still name the version the plan actually used, or the latest? The card must name what the plan was BUILT ON. Where an answer is 'not covered', add it to the owning child's DoD or as a comment here — do not file a new evidence row (global rail 21).

(a) THE DESIGN IS LOAD-BEARING, in two different shapes per lane. NODE lane carries the entity NAME into the bytes: aggregate `revision.dataModel[*].entity` -> `entityNames()` (wrapper-mission-inputs.ts:63) -> `DesignBrief.entities` -> `nodeDesignLines` renders `entities User`. The committed arm (wrapper-mission-inputs.test.ts:102-119) reads the entity OFF the fixture record rather than retyping it, so a fixture edit cannot leave it green. COMPILER lane deliberately carries the REF plus the five DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS and the `design_read` fetch verb, not the entity names — the sections are large and task-7f9f20c7 published the MCP kind to fetch them. Not a form the plan ignores.

(b) THE LOOP CAN ALWAYS REACH A PLAN, AND THERE IS ONE REAL GAP I am recording rather than filing. The skip path compiles: affordance-read-planning.test.ts:1256 shows a skipped goal offers exactly {planning.submit_decomposition}, compiles, and reaches approval.decide_intent. BUT after Gate 1 with no design and no skip, the surface offers exactly {design.submit} and WITHHOLDS planning.submit_decomposition (:1204; the filter at :1169-1173 covers both kinds, so this is real withholding). The design step is a hard gate on decomposition until designed-or-skipped. The fleet clears it automatically (wrapper staffs design.submit at rank 1). The gap: `grep -rn 'design\.submit' apps/control-room/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` = ZERO HITS — no browser surface dispatches it, so the skip is READ by the UI (design-card renders "The design step was skipped. <reason>") but not WRITABLE from it. An operator with no design seat available has no button to declare "plan without a design". Not a permanent wedge (any authenticated principal can dispatch; the affordance offer exists) and not a blocker for this roll-up — recorded as a comment per global rail 21, NOT as a new evidence row.

(c) THE SKIP IS STATED ON BOTH SIDES, never a silent absence. Compiler mission: "NO DESIGN EXISTS ... BECAUSE THE DESIGN STEP WAS SKIPPED ... do not wait for a design that is never coming", with an explicit `not.toContain("NO DESIGN ACCOMPANIES")` so skip never collapses into absence. Approval card: design-version-note.test.tsx:54-67 says SKIPPED with the reason and asserts no "Design version" string. DesignBrief is PRESENT|SKIPPED|UNREADABLE|ABSENT and UNREADABLE carries code AND layer on both lanes (DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE@LEDGER compiler-side, DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED@LEDGER node-side), so a seat cannot confuse "the operator skipped" with "the read failed".

(d) THE CARD AND THE NODE NAME WHAT THE PLAN WAS BUILT ON, not the latest. Decisive arm wrapper-mission-inputs.test.ts:184-198: design v1, COMPILE, then publish v2 — node bytes contain @v1, `not.toContain("@v2")`, and `not.toContain("Session")` (the entity v2 added); the same arm asserts the compiler correctly reads LATEST (@v2) because a compiler seat is staffed before any plan exists. Card side: LiveDesignVersionNote reads BY THE PLANNING RUN and design-version-note.test.tsx:99-118 asserts the selector actually REACHES the reader; design-store.ts:196-198 resolves it via readCompiledContractBinding and answers DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED rather than falling back to latest.
